feature.label: Ijams Park
feature.title: Shakespeare's closing weekend at Ijams Park — last chances, and a free Thursday
feature.deck: Both plays trade nights one more time, Thursday's Henry V is pay-what-you-can, and Sunday moves indoors for a Merry Wives double-header before the festival packs up.

facts.label: Sun Jul 26
facts.value: Merry Wives — 2 PM matinee & 7:30 PM, both indoors

facts.label: Where
facts.value: Visitor Center lawn, Ijams Park, 2915 Island Home Ave

facts.label: Bring
facts.value: A lawn chair or blanket · parking free 30 min before

body.text: If you kept meaning to get out to Shakespeare at Ijams Park and never did, this is the weekend the window closes. The Tennessee Stage Company's thirty-sixth festival plays its final four nights on the lawn, with King Henry V and The Merry Wives of Windsor trading places one last time.

The move to make is Thursday. Henry V — the big, rousing one, Agincourt and the St. Crispin's Day speech — is the week's pay-what-you-can night, so it costs whatever you decide. Bring a chair or a blanket, because the lawn is the seating, and parking's free starting thirty minutes before the 7:30 curtain. Kids under fifteen get in free through Penny for the Arts. Everyone else, twenty dollars.

Friday brings the comedy, Merry Wives, and Saturday swings back to Henry V. Then Sunday the whole thing moves indoors to the Visitor Center for a proper send-off: a two o'clock matinee and a 7:30 evening show, both of them Merry Wives — Falstaff getting his comeuppance twice in one day. If it rains any night, the Visitor Center is the backup, so weather isn't automatically a washout.

One small heads-up from the box office of experience: the online ticket page has been a little inconsistent on price from night to night. If a screen quotes you something odd, twenty is the number, and 865-546-4280 settles anything else.

stories.label: Old Sevier
stories.imageCaption: The date on the contract: this week
stories.title: Sevier Avenue's roadway was due this week. It didn't make it.
stories.deck: The contract to rebuild the corridor and its new roundabout carried a completion date of July 21. The city has quietly extended it — and the Kerbela apartments, meanwhile, are still stuck in committee.

facts.label: Utility work
facts.value: A separate contract runs to Sept 30

body.text: Here is a date worth marking: July 21, this past Tuesday, was the contract completion date for the Sevier Avenue roadway project — the big rebuild that includes the new roundabout at Sevier, Foggy Bottom, and Island Home. If you've driven it lately, you already know it isn't finished. The city's own July status report confirms it: crews are still working the drainage system on the south side and making their way west, and, in the report's quiet phrasing, "the contract time was extended."

That's not a scandal — big streetscape jobs slip, and this one has to hand off between a roadway contractor and a separate utility-undergrounding crew whose own work runs into the fall. But it's worth saying plainly, because the city has floated "early 2027" for the roundabout, and a deadline that arrives and passes without much fanfare is exactly the kind of thing the Ear is here to notice.

And a mile up the hill, the other South Knoxville land-use story we've been tracking hasn't moved either. The roughly 220-unit apartment plan for the old Kerbela Shriners Temple site was remanded back to the Administrative Review Committee two weeks ago — and it still hasn't been rescheduled. It's not on the Planning Commission's next agenda, August 13. For now, the bluff waits.

stories.label: Suttree Landing
stories.title: There's a new brunch room on the river: Mimosas
stories.deck: At the corner of Blount and Chapman, on the ground floor of The Davy, Mimosas has been quietly pouring bottomless brunch since the fall. Consider this your introduction.

facts.label: Where
facts.value: 222 E. Blount Ave — ground floor of The Davy, at Blount & Chapman

body.text: Not everything in this week's Ear is happening for the first time this weekend — some of it has just been waiting for us to catch up. Mimosas opened last November on the ground floor of The Davy, the apartment high-rise at Blount Avenue and Chapman Highway, and somehow we haven't sent you there yet. Fixing that now.

It's an all-day brunch-and-cocktails room from Kennedy Concepts — the group behind Cafe 4 and The Kennedy downtown — built around exactly what the name promises. Bottomless mimosas on the weekend, five-dollar mimosas and six-dollar Bloody Marys any day, and a proper brunch menu Saturday and Sunday from nine to three. There's a happy hour on weekdays, three to six, if a Tuesday needs saving.

One housekeeping note, because we like to get these right: the address turns up two ways online — 222 East Blount Avenue in most listings, a Mimosa Avenue number on a couple of others. It's the ground floor of The Davy at Blount and Chapman; you'll find it. A quick call to 865-357-7020 confirms a table.

stories.label: Kern's
stories.imageCaption: The screen comes down, the band plugs in
stories.title: Kern's trades the World Cup big screen for a hoedown
stories.deck: With the tournament over, the food hall fills the weekend the old-fashioned way: a Friday-night Ho'Down Social and live music straight through Sunday.

facts.label: Fri Jul 24
facts.value: Corey Clifton Band 5 PM · Ho'Down Social 8–11 PM

body.text: For a month, the big outdoor screen at Kern's was the neighborhood's World Cup living room. The tournament wrapped Sunday, and rather than go quiet, the food hall leaned into what it does the rest of the year — a weekend of live music with a barn dance bolted on.

Friday's the anchor: the Corey Clifton Band plays a rock set from five to a quarter of eight, timed to hand straight off to the Kern's Ho'Down Social at eight — line dancing, boots, the works, on the Scruff stage till eleven. Saturday brings a candle-making class in the afternoon and Rossdafareye's loopy "Appalachian space funk" at six. And Sunday winds down easy with the Chattanooga duo Kaylee Brooks and Levi Ouimet, country covers and originals, one to four.

A quick correction to your muscle memory, since Kern's runs a lot of weekly specials: several of the summer standbys have rolled off the calendar, so don't count on the tournament-season lineup. The music, though, is on.

stories.label: Old Sevier
stories.title: Emo drag, Sunday bluegrass, and a stained-glass class
stories.deck: The Sevier Avenue breweries carry the weekend's nightlife: Hi-Wire goes emo on Saturday, Alliance goes bluegrass on Sunday, and there's a suncatcher to make in between.

facts.label: Sat Jul 25
facts.value: Hi-Wire — Panic! At the Drag Show (emo drag night) · 9 PM · 18+

facts.label: Sun Jul 26
facts.value: Hi-Wire — Intro to Stained Glass · 2–4 PM · $80

facts.label: Where
facts.value: Hi-Wire 2020 Barber St · Alliance 1130 Sevier Ave

body.text: Saturday night, Hi-Wire on Barber Street throws "Panic! At the Drag Show" — an emo-themed drag night, nine to close, eighteen and up, eight bucks in advance. It is exactly as much fun as it sounds, and precisely the kind of thing that makes a brewery district a neighborhood.

Sunday slows the tempo way down. Hi-Wire hosts an Intro to Stained Glass workshop from two to four — you leave with a copper-foil suncatcher, eighty dollars, all materials in, ages fourteen up. And around the corner, Alliance Brewing on Sevier Avenue has the Breadlosers playing free bluegrass at four, all ages, the kind of easy Sunday-afternoon set you can bring the porch energy to.
Between the two rooms that's a full weekend of Old Sevier nightlife without repeating yourself once.

stories.label: Suttree Landing
stories.title: Earl's runs the margarita clock again
stories.deck: The waterfront happy hour holds: Patrón mango margaritas Thursday, the spicy pineapple ritas back Friday, both 4 to 6.

facts.label: Both
facts.value: 4–6 PM · $1 off liquor, beer & wine (excludes daily specials)

body.text: Earl's keeps its weekday happy-hour rhythm on the waterfront. Thursday it's ten-dollar Patrón mango margaritas; Friday the spicy pineapple ritas we told you about last week are back at nine, both in the four-to-six window, both with a dollar off liquor, beer, and wine on the side. Daily specials excepted, as always.
And the same handy fact still applies: Friday's happy hour lets out at six, ninety minutes before Shakespeare's curtain up the road. Some plans just build themselves.

stories.label: Ijams Park
stories.imageCaption: The quiet half of the park's weekend
stories.title: Beyond the stage: paddles, storytelling, and the banders are back
stories.deck: The rest of Ijams Park keeps its own weekend — two evening paddles, a Saturday of stories and skills, and Sunday's bird-banding table returning at dawn.

facts.label: Sun Jul 26
facts.value: Bird Banding 7:30 AM · Self Care Sunday yoga 11:30 AM

body.text: While the Bard has the lawn, the rest of Ijams Park runs its usual gentle slate. Friday and Saturday both offer a guided Evening Paddle at 7:30, sunset on the Tennessee River with boats provided — register ahead. Saturday fills in around it: free storytelling at the Nature Playscape from ten to noon, and a three-hour Wilderness Basics class in the afternoon for anyone who wants to be a little more capable outdoors.

But the one to circle is Sunday at 7:30 in the morning, when the bird-banding table is back after a couple of weeks off. Researchers net, measure, band, and release wild songbirds close enough to count the feathers — real science, all ages, coffee encouraged. And if you'd rather ease in, Self Care Sunday yoga is in the trees at 11:30.
